text:
incident-bot: 🔔 Pager triggered: high 5xx rate from api-gateway (edge) — threshold breach at 1733333333. Current 5xx: 18% (5m), baseline 0.6%. Alert ID: PDR-9821.
oncall-sre-lee: on it. paging into #incidents and #eng-oncall. grabbing initial telemetry.
eng-platform-maya: jumping in — which regions affected?
oncall-sre-lee: looks like eu-west-1 and us-west-2 edge proxies. eu-west is worse. latency spikes correlate with 502/504s.
infra-nick: checking upstream host pools now. seeing increased connection resets from our edge -> api-gw pool. possible backend timeouts.
support-jordan: already seeing customer tickets for failed uploads (S3 proxied flows). marking high customer impact.
product-ryan: customers with streaming sessions might be impacted too. need quick comms if this persists.
eng-platform-maya: can we toggle fallback routing to older stable ingress?
oncall-sre-lee: plan: 1) throttle bursty clients at WAF level 2) flip routing to standby gateway variant in us-west-2 3) raise timeouts upstream 4) enable degraded-mode for streaming. execute steps?
infra-nick: working on step 1 now — creating WAF rate-limit rule for path /api/v1/generate (attack-mode). will apply to offending ASNs first.
eng-platform-maya: prepare a canary route to standby: kubectl apply -f /manifests/gateway-standby-canary.yaml (I will paste).
eng-platform-maya: ```
# canary routing snippet
apiVersion: networking/v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-standby-canary
spec:
  selector:
    app: api-gateway-standby
  ports:
  - port: 443
```
oncall-sre-lee: infra-nick — once WAF rule is live, I'll shift 10% of traffic via canary then 50%. keep an eye on 5xx%.
infra-nick: WAF rule deployed (aid: waf-2039). blocking top 40 client IPs by rate-limit. immediate delta: 5xx dropped to 14% in eu-west.
support-jordan: posting to status: "Intermittent 502/504 errors for some API requests; engineering investigating." draft ready.
product-ryan: yes publish with note about 'partial regional impact' and advise retry/backoff.
oncall-sre-lee: initiating canary switch now: `kubectl set image deployment/gateway primary=api-gateway:v2-standby --namespace=infra` (10%).
deploy-bot: deploy started by eng-platform-maya at 1733333430. CI checks green.
eng-platform-maya: 10% route confirmed. eu-west 5xx -> 9% now. us-west steady at 12%.
infra-nick: upstream pool logs: increased 502s correlate with steady increase in connection queue lengths on nodes gw-uw2-a03 and gw-ew1-b05. suspect slow backend instances causing head-of-line blocking.
oncall-sre-lee: can we spin temporary extra replicas for backend service 'model-proxy' in us-west-2?
eng-platform-maya: scaling model-proxy +3 in us-west-2: `kubectl scale deploy/model-proxy --replicas=9 -n services-usw2`. doing it.
infra-nick: scaled. new pods coming up; health checks flapping on first two due to disk pressure, but passing soon.
eng-platform-maya: increase upstream timeout from 10s -> 20s for gateway so it doesn't return 504s on transient load: `env GATEWAY_TIMEOUT=20s` rolling restart.
support-jordan: updated status: "Partial recovery after mitigation steps; traffic shifted to standby gateway and autoscaling initiated. Some customers still experience intermittent failures — we'll provide updates." :thumbsup:
product-ryan: prepare a customer-facing postmortem stub capturing timeline, affected endpoints, and recommended retry behavior.
oncall-sre-lee: monitoring: after canary and scale+timeout change eu-west 5xx down to 4.3%, us-west to 5.1%. still seeing small spike at 1733333600 — investigating root cause for initial storm.
infra-nick: pulling edge logs for suspicious connection patterns. noticed sudden increase in chunked POSTs from a small set of clients; likely buggy retry logic causing amplified load.
eng-platform-maya: let's enable circuit-breaker to fail-fast when backend queue depth > 200 to avoid cascading 502s. Patching LB policy now.
oncall-sre-lee: circuit breaker applied. new metric shows early rejects rather than timeouts, which is healthier. 5xx trending down to 1.9% cluster-wide.
support-jordan: triage notes: impacted customers (IDs): C-10024, C-10079, C-10345 — support reached out to premium customers.
product-ryan: request a short proactive email for enterprise customers summarizing the issue and mitigations. Jordan to coordinate.
support-jordan: will send draft. need exact ETA for full recovery?
oncall-sre-lee: ETA ~15-20 minutes to stabilize, keep oncall for 1 hour post-stable.
eng-platform-maya: root cause hypothesis: sudden client-side retry storms + a couple of overloaded backend nodes combined with conservative timeouts. recommended follow-ups: 1) long-term circuit-breaker tuning 2) rate-limit rules for uploads 3) investigate client SDK retry behavior 4) add better autoscaling SLO for model-proxy.
infra-nick: saving logs and opening incident ticket: INC-2024-1733333333 with attach: gw-logs.tar.gz.
support-jordan: customer comms queued, will send after final confirmation.
oncall-sre-lee: handing off to eng-platform-maya for post-incident wrap. summary: mitigation executed (WAF rate-limit, traffic canary, scale model-proxy, bump timeout, circuit-breaker). customer impact: high for a subset of users (uploads/streaming) for ~12 minutes.
eng-platform-maya: taking post-incident. I'll run through RCA checklist and assign follow-ups. thanks team. :raised_hands:
support-jordan: closing paging ticket but keeping incident channel open for wrap.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-1733333333 resolved at 1733333620 — status: mitigated.
eng-platform-maya: quick notes for postmortem: include metrics snapshots (5xx/latency), list of customers impacted, exact timeline of config changes, and a reproduction plan for the retry storm.
product-ryan: will join RCA sync at 1733334000 to plan customer comms cadence.
oncall-sre-lee: thumbs up. moving to post-incident ops.
